meta.title: Silica Station

subtitle.short: Keep your Moon crew alive for 12 rounds.
subtitle.detail: You are the Mission Commander at Shackleton Crater on the Moon's South Pole. Every button shows what you lose right away, and what comes back 3 rounds later.

location.detail: Shackleton Crater sits near the lunar south pole, where crater rims catch long sunlight while dark crater floors trap ancient water ice.

moonDirtNote.detail: Lunar regolith is crushed rock and dust covering the Moon. It contains trapped oxygen atoms in silicate minerals and can be piled up as thick walls to block space radiation.

powerAtZeroRule.short: Power at 0 stops air machines (-15 extra oxygen).
powerAtZeroRule.detail: Life-support fans and oxygen scrubbers need electricity to run. If station power hits 0, the crew loses an extra 15 oxygen every round until power is restored.

meta.darkPeriodNote: Note: The 14-day lunar night is simplified to 5 night rounds (Rounds 5–9) so students can complete a full mission in ~8 minutes.

chapters.title: Establish the Station
chapters.summary: Turn on station systems, manage batteries, and divide your moon dirt.

chapters.title: Prepare for Lunar Night
chapters.summary: Get ready before darkness cuts off solar power and supply ships fall behind.

chapters.title: Survive the Crisis
chapters.summary: Weather the dark period, fix shortages, and shield the crew from a solar flare.

chapters.title: Recover and Complete Mission
chapters.summary: Bring solar power back online, steady the crew, and reach the resupply ship.

night_soon.short: Dark night starts in 2 rounds! Solar power stops.
night_soon.detail: During lunar night, solar panels produce 0 power. Save battery power before Round 5 begins.

delay_soon.short: Supply ship is late! Arrives 2 rounds behind.
delay_soon.detail: The Earth cargo rocket had a launch delay. You will need to stretch your food or emergency air in Round 6.

flare_soon.short: Solar flare hits in 2 rounds! Check your shield.
flare_soon.detail: A burst of high-energy solar particles is racing toward the Moon. Moon dirt shielding and shelter power will cut the radiation damage in Round 8.

leak_soon.short: Small air leak detected! Fix it before it grows.
leak_soon.detail: A tiny seal on the airlock is hissing. Patching it early costs a little moon dirt, while ignoring it costs much more oxygen later.

title.short: Choose how to use Moon Dirt
title.detail: You have a limited pile of lunar regolith (moon dirt). Pick ONE job for 15 units of moon dirt—the other two jobs will have to wait. The result arrives in 3 rounds.

situation.short: 15 moon dirt can make Air, Shield, or Batteries.
situation.detail: Every choice uses 15 moon dirt right away and delivers its reward three rounds later. Think ahead about what danger is coming next!

label.detail: Bake lunar regolith to release trapped oxygen for the crew.

why.short: Gives +36 oxygen in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Lunar soil is roughly 40% oxygen by weight, locked in rock minerals. Baking it gives the crew +36 oxygen 3 rounds later—vital because you start with 85 oxygen and 12 rounds burn 144!

delayedReason.short: Moon dirt became +36 oxygen, so the crew can breathe longer.
delayedReason.detail: Oxygen extraction finished! +36 oxygen was pumped into the station's air tanks.

choices.teaches: Moon dirt can be baked into breathable oxygen, but it uses soil needed for shielding.

label.detail: Pile lunar regolith over the habitat roof to block solar radiation.

why.short: Adds +15 shield in 3 rounds (max 30 counts).
why.detail: The Moon has no thick air or magnetic field to stop solar storms. Piling moon dirt adds +15 shield in 3 rounds. Note: Only 30 shield points count against a flare, so a 3rd shield pick is wasted!

delayedReason.short: Moon dirt in the shield blocks radiation, like a thick wall.
delayedReason.detail: Regolith shielding layer completed! +15 radiation shield added to the habitat roof.

choices.teaches: Thick moon dirt blocks space radiation, up to the station's 30-point cap.

label.detail: Sinter moon dirt into bricks for an extra battery bay.

why.short: Gives +15 power and +15 max battery in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Building a larger battery bay increases your station's power storage limit from 100 to 115 and delivers +15 power in 3 rounds to survive the dark night.

delayedReason.short: New battery box built: +15 power and +15 battery cap.
delayedReason.detail: Construction finished! Your maximum battery storage grew by 15 and gained +15 stored power.

choices.teaches: Expanding battery capacity prepares the station for long periods without sunlight.

title.detail: Lunar temperatures plunge below -130°C in shadows. Keeping the cabin warm uses power right now, while turning heaters off risks crew illness 3 rounds later.

situation.short: Keep heaters ON, or save power by turning OFF?
situation.detail: Keeping heaters ON costs 15 power immediately. Turning them OFF saves power right now, but cold air makes an astronaut sick three rounds later (-18 health, -6 O₂) and drains -5 health & -6 O₂ every round while sick.

label.detail: Run cabin heaters to keep the crew warm and healthy.

why.short: Safe temperature—no sickness in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Prevention is cheaper than a cure! Spending 15 power now keeps cabin air warm so nobody gets sick later.

delayedReason.short: The heating stayed on, so the crew stayed warm.
delayedReason.detail: Stable cabin temperatures kept all astronauts healthy with zero cold stress.

choices.teaches: Keeping life support heaters running protects crew health.

label.detail: Shut down cabin heaters to save battery power right now.

choices.costLabel: Free now · -18 health & -6 O₂ in 3 rounds

why.short: Saves power now, but -18 health & sickness (-5 health/rd) later.
why.detail: Switching heating OFF freezes air scrubbers (-6 oxygen), makes an astronaut sick (-18 health, plus -5 health & -6 oxygen/rd while untreated), and treating them later costs 25 power and 10 moon dirt!

delayedReason.short: The heating was off: someone got sick (-18 health, -6 O₂).
delayedReason.detail: Freezing cabin air chilled the crew (-18 health) and iced up scrubber vents (-6 oxygen). Untreated illness drains -5 health and -6 oxygen every round!

choices.teaches: Skipping heating saves power today but causes costly illness, health loss, and oxygen loss later.

title.detail: Tiny sharp grains of lunar dust stick to solar panels like static cling, blocking sunlight if not brushed off.

situation.short: Clean the dusty solar panels, or skip it?
situation.detail: Electrostatic lunar dust coats the solar wings. Sending the wiper arm costs 5 power now, while skipping cleaning cuts solar power by 10/rd and loses 15 power in 3 rounds.

label.detail: Save power right now and leave the dust on the panels.

choices.costLabel: Free now · -15 power & dusty solar later

why.short: Saves 5 power now, loses 15 power in 3 rounds + blocks sun.
why.detail: Leaving dust on the panels blocks sunlight (-10 solar power on sunny rounds) and causes static buildup that drains 15 power in 3 rounds.

delayedReason.short: Dust covered the solar panels (-15 power).
delayedReason.detail: Thick lunar dust shaded the solar wings, draining 15 power from the station grid.

choices.teaches: Skipping small maintenance causes bigger power losses later.

label.detail: Brush dust off the solar arrays so sunlight hits every cell.

why.short: Costs 5 power now to prevent -15 power & lost sunlight.
why.detail: Lunar dust is jagged and electrically charged, so it clings tightly to glass. Cleaning takes just 5 power now and avoids losing 15 power and solar charging later.

delayedReason.short: Clean panels kept solar electricity flowing strong.
delayedReason.detail: Because the dust was brushed off early, the solar arrays run at full efficiency.

choices.teaches: Lunar dust sticks to everything and blocks sunlight.

title.detail: The resupply rocket from Earth was delayed on the launchpad. You must stretch supplies right now.

situation.short: Rocket is late! Eat less food, or tap emergency air?
situation.detail: Neither option costs anything today, because the shortage hits 3 rounds from now. Choose which reserve to stretch.

label.detail: Keep full meals for crew health, and burn backup air canisters.

why.short: Protects health, but costs 25 oxygen later.
why.detail: Keeping meals normal keeps crew health steady, but using backup reserves drops oxygen by 25 three rounds later—risking oxygen depletion!

delayedReason.short: The ship was late, so backup air ran down (-25 oxygen).
delayedReason.detail: Emergency air tanks dropped (-25 oxygen) while waiting for the delayed rocket.

choices.teaches: Emergency reserves keep the crew fed, but shrink your oxygen margin.

label.detail: Ration astronaut meals so emergency oxygen tanks stay full.

why.short: Protects oxygen, but crew loses 18 health later.
why.detail: Cutting meal calories saves your emergency air canisters, but underfed astronauts lose strength and immune health (-18 health in 3 rounds).

delayedReason.short: The ship was late, so smaller meals lowered health (-18).
delayedReason.detail: Rationing food stretched supplies until resupply, costing 18 crew health.

choices.teaches: Supply delays force commanders to trade between crew health and oxygen.

label.detail: Power the hydroponic lunar farm to grow fresh food and recycle cabin air.

choices.costLabel: Costs 5 power now · +32 O₂ & +6 health later

why.short: Trades 5 power now for +32 oxygen and +6 health in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Inspired by the Canadian Space Agency's Lunar Food program: energy-saving LED plants turn carbon dioxide into +32 breathable oxygen while supplying fresh vitamins.

delayedReason.short: CSA Greenhouse crops boosted health (+6) and air (+32 oxygen)!
delayedReason.detail: CSA-style Controlled Environment Agriculture produced fresh greens and recycled +32 oxygen for the crew.

choices.teaches: Space greenhouses grow nutritious food while helping recycle breathable oxygen.

title.detail: One crew member caught an illness from the cold cabin earlier. Treating them now costs heavy power and moon dirt, while leaving them untreated keeps draining oxygen every round.

situation.short: A crew member is sick! Treat now or let them rest?
situation.detail: Medical bay equipment needs 25 power and 10 moon dirt right away (+15 health). Leaving it untreated spreads illness (-20 health later) and keeps draining -5 health & -6 oxygen/rd.

label.detail: Save power and moon dirt, and hope the crew recovers on its own.

why.short: Saves supplies now, but illness worsens (-20 health + -5 health/rd).
why.detail: Inside a sealed lunar cabin, germs spread through recycled air. Without treatment, crew health drops 20 points and loses another 5 health and 6 oxygen every round.

delayedReason.short: Untreated illness spread through the cabin (-20 health).
delayedReason.detail: Without med-bay treatment, illness worsened (-20 health) and drained crew health and oxygen every round.

choices.teaches: Untreated problems inside a closed habitat spread to the whole crew.

label.detail: Run the med-bay purifier and heal the sick crew member.

why.short: Restores +15 health now, stops illness & extra O₂ drain.
why.detail: Curing an illness on the Moon costs 25 power and 10 moon dirt—much more than keeping the heating on earlier!

delayedReason.short: Early medical treatment cured the crew completely.
delayedReason.detail: The med-bay cleared the infection and stopped the extra oxygen drain.

choices.teaches: Prevention is much cheaper than curing sickness in space.

title.detail: A storm of high-energy protons from the Sun is hitting Silica Station right now! Your Round 5 moon dirt choice lands first, then the flare strikes.

situation.short: Radiation storm! Take shelter or keep working?
situation.detail: Using the shelter costs 20 power and cuts whatever flare damage gets past your shield in HALF. Keeping work going saves power, but takes full flare damage plus -5 health later.

label.detail: Move the whole crew into the shielded storm shelter.

why.short: Cuts flare damage in HALF! Safe in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Running air scrubbers inside the tight storm bunker costs 20 power, but cuts remaining solar flare damage in half and avoids delayed radiation fatigue.

delayedReason.short: Sheltering under moon dirt blocked the solar storm.
delayedReason.detail: Because the crew stayed inside the shelter, they avoided delayed radiation sickness.

choices.teaches: Taking shelter combines with moon dirt walls to protect astronauts from flares.

label.detail: Save 20 power and keep station tasks running during the storm.

choices.costLabel: Free now · Full flare + -15 health later

why.short: Takes full flare damage now (up to -45), plus -15 health later.
why.detail: Saves 20 power, but the crew absorbs full unshielded flare damage right now AND suffers -15 delayed radiation fatigue 3 rounds later.

delayedReason.short: Solar flare work caused delayed radiation fatigue (-15 health).
delayedReason.detail: High-energy particles caused tiredness and radiation sickness (-15 health).

choices.teaches: Working through a solar storm risks immediate and delayed radiation harm.

title.detail: The Moon has only 1/6th of Earth's gravity. Without daily exercise, astronaut bones and heart muscles quickly weaken.

situation.short: Run exercise machines, or skip workout?
situation.detail: Powering the treadmill and resistance gear uses 10 power today. Skipping saves power now, but costs 10 health during the resupply check-up!

label.detail: Conserve 10 power and let the crew skip workouts.

why.short: Saves 10 power now, costs 10 health in check-up.
why.detail: Even in the final rounds, late shortcuts come back! Skipping exercise weakens the crew by -10 health before the final score.

delayedReason.short: Skipping exercise weakened muscles in low gravity (-10 health).
delayedReason.detail: Low Moon gravity drained crew strength (-10 health) during the final resupply check-up.

choices.teaches: Even late mission shortcuts affect your final crew health.

label.detail: Keep crew muscles and bones strong in 1/6th Moon gravity.

why.short: Costs 10 power now, protects crew for resupply.
why.detail: NASA astronauts exercise 2 hours every day in space so their bodies stay strong enough to handle landing back on Earth.

delayedReason.short: Daily exercise kept crew muscles strong for landing.
delayedReason.detail: Astronauts passed their final strength check when the resupply spacecraft docked.

choices.teaches: Low gravity weakens bones and muscles without regular exercise.

title.short: Rover Ice Hunt at Crater Edge
title.detail: Cold shadows inside Shackleton Crater hold frozen water ice. Sending the rover costs power now, and splits ice into oxygen 3 rounds later.

situation.short: Send the rover to dig lunar ice, or keep it docked?
situation.detail: Driving into the freezing crater shadow uses 20 power right away, but turns mined ice into +32 oxygen in 3 rounds.

label.detail: Mine frozen water in crater shadows and split it into oxygen.

why.short: Gives +32 oxygen in 3 rounds!
why.detail: NASA targets the Moon's South Pole because crater ice (H₂O) can be melted and split with electricity into +32 breathable oxygen!

delayedReason.short: Crater ice was melted and split into +32 oxygen.
delayedReason.detail: Rover returned with pure ice from Shackleton Crater, boosting oxygen by 32.

choices.teaches: South Pole water ice can become drinking water and breathable air.

label.detail: Save 20 power and rely on your current oxygen tanks.

why.short: Saves 20 power immediately.
why.detail: If your oxygen is already safe and power is tight, keeping the rover docked protects your battery reserves.

delayedReason.short: Rover stayed docked to preserve battery reserves.
delayedReason.detail: Batteries stayed charged, though no extra crater ice was harvested.

choices.teaches: Every expedition trades battery power for future supplies.

title.detail: A tiny crack in the habitat seal is leaking air into the Moon's vacuum. Patching it now costs 5 moon dirt; ignoring it loses 18 oxygen in 3 rounds.

situation.short: Patch the hissing air leak, or ignore it?
situation.detail: Mixing moon dirt sealant costs 5 moon dirt right now. Ignoring the leak saves dirt today, but loses 18 oxygen three rounds later.

label.detail: Seal the crack with moon dirt glue before air escapes.

why.short: Stops a -18 oxygen leak in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Small problems grow fast in a vacuum! Spending 5 moon dirt now saves 18 breathable oxygen later.

delayedReason.short: Patched airlock held tight with zero air lost.
delayedReason.detail: The early seal repair stopped the leak completely.

choices.teaches: Fixing small problems early saves vital resources later.

label.detail: Save moon dirt now and let the airlock keep hissing.

why.short: Saves 5 dirt now, loses 18 oxygen in 3 rounds.
why.detail: Pressure leaks widen over time. By 3 rounds from now, 18 oxygen will escape into space.

delayedReason.short: Unpatched air leak vented 18 oxygen into space.
delayedReason.detail: The ignored crack grew wider and drained 18 oxygen from the cabin.

choices.teaches: Small problems grow if ignored.

flareHit.detail: Radiation hit the habitat. Your moon dirt shield and shelter cut down the damage.

resupplyArrived.detail: Fresh oxygen, food, and replacement parts arrived from Earth. Final check-up complete!

powerZeroPenalty.short: Power hit 0! Air machines stopped (-15 extra oxygen).
powerZeroPenalty.detail: Without electricity, life-support scrubbers shut down and oxygen fell by an extra 15.
